module.title: Natural-language analytics with Genie
module.summary: Place Genie One, Genie Agents and Genie Code by role, follow one question to a validated answer, curate a space that keeps answers on the metric contract under each asker's permissions, and benchmark it without claiming a live result.
objectives: Distinguish the Genie family's roles and read each documentation page's own name for them.
Curate a Genie Agent with few described tables, SQL semantics, example SQL, specific instructions and trusted assets, and trace where a wrong answer started.
Write a benchmark with guarded classes and a review loop, run as each audience's identity, kept apart from any live-agent claim.

scenarios.title: Decide whether Cinderline's Genie Agent is ready for every North supervisor
scenarios.context: Fictional Cinderline Components' plant analyst demoed the North plant quality Genie Agent to the operations director, who wants all North supervisors on it next Monday. The space holds the accepted daily line-rate table and the exclusion counts, a metric view for unit_defect_rate, three example queries, one trusted SQL function and four instructions. A 24-question benchmark was authored against the five-day synthetic snapshot; its run log is empty. The demo used the analyst's own account.
scenarios.task: Write a one-page readiness note for the operations director: what the space covers and does not, what the demo does and does not show, the benchmark runs required before rollout and with which identities, the failure classes and the change each leads to, and a recommendation with its conditions.
requirements: Separate the authored benchmark and the demo from any evidence about how the live space answers supervisors.
Name the test identities for each run and why the analyst's own account cannot stand in for them.
Map each failure class to one curation change and name the class that stops the rollout.
State what the space cannot answer and how supervisors will be told.
scenarios.model:
### What the space covers
North plant line rates by business day from accepted inspections, with withheld and quarantined counts; the unit_defect_rate measure is defined once in a metric view as a ratio of sums. It does not hold causes, sensor data, other plants, forecasts or a rework rule.

### What the demo shows
That the space can answer a handful of questions for the analyst's account, which can read quarantine data supervisors cannot. It says nothing about supervisors' answers, ambiguous words or unauthorized requests.

### Required before rollout
Run the 24-question benchmark as a test supervisor identity and a test analyst identity, with the unauthorized cases as test-outsider (space access, no SELECT), dated, with the space's configuration and snapshot recorded. Classify failures: wrong table (scope or descriptions), wrong filter (example SQL), wrong arithmetic (metric view), false confidence or missing clarification (specific instruction). Any unauthorized row stops the rollout and goes to the access review.

### Recommendation
Not ready for Monday. Ready when both identity runs pass every guarded class and at least the aggregate and ratio classes, with the run log attached. Supervisors are told in the space's opening text what it cannot answer.
scenarios.reasoning: The note refuses to treat a curator-account demo as evidence, turns the authored benchmark into a dated, identity-specific run, ties every failure to one change, and gives the director a conditional yes with a date-independent test rather than a promise.

rubric.weak: Calls the space tested because the demo went well.
rubric.partial: Mentions the benchmark but treats the authored expectations as results.
rubric.strong: Separates demo, authored benchmark and dated runs, and claims only what a run shows.

rubric.weak: No identities named; the curator's account is assumed representative.
rubric.partial: Names a supervisor test identity but not why the analyst's account differs.
rubric.strong: Names each audience's test identity, explains embedded warehouse credentials versus per-user data access, and stops on any disclosure.

rubric.weak: Proposes more instructions for every failure.
rubric.partial: Classifies failures but maps several to the same instruction.
rubric.strong: Maps each class to its documented input (scope, example SQL, metric view, specific instruction) and keeps disclosure out of curation.

rubric.weak: Promises the space can answer supervisors' questions generally.
rubric.partial: Lists limits but gives an unconditional yes or no.
rubric.strong: States what cannot be answered and how supervisors learn it, and gives a conditional recommendation tied to named runs.

disclosures.question: Which account did the demo use?
disclosures.response: The analyst's own; it has SELECT on the quarantine schema, which supervisors do not.

disclosures.question: Has anyone run the benchmark in the space?
disclosures.response: No. The 24 questions and their reference answers exist in a spreadsheet; the run log is empty.

claims.description: Genie is a family: Genie One for business users, Genie Agents as domain-specific environments that turn questions into SQL, and Genie Code for developers.

The Genie Agents page says agents were formerly Genie Spaces; several pages under /genie/ still say Genie Space; the older trusted-assets page says AI/BI Genie spaces; Genie One was previously Databricks One.
claims.context: Page titles confirmed by search on 2026-09-23.

claims.description: Curation guidance ranks documented datasets, SQL expressions for semantics, example SQL, then text instructions as a last resort; it recommends five or fewer tables, prejoined views or metric views, and specific instructions; Genie uses Unity Catalog names and descriptions.
Unity Catalog metric views define a measure once, separately from grouping fields, and can be queried by Genie Agents, dashboards and SQL.
Parameterized example queries and SQL functions are trusted assets; a response built from a parameterized example's exact text is labelled Trusted; users need EXECUTE on trusted functions.
A Genie Agent's results are governed by each user's own Unity Catalog permissions; the author's embedded compute credentials grant warehouse access only; row filters and column masks apply per user.
claims.context: Create and manage a Genie Agent page.

claims.description: When Genie cannot answer it might ask a clarification question or explain that it cannot answer from the provided information.

Genie benchmarks compare generated SQL and results with a SQL answer, need manual review without one, and should include two to four phrasings of a question; the Monitor tab shows feedback and review requests.
claims.context: The product features; the course ran none.

concepts.definition: Genie One for business users, Genie Agents for curated domains and Genie Code for developers, over Unity Catalog.
A curated domain environment that turns natural-language questions into SQL run under each asker's permissions.
Question, interpretation, generated SQL, result and validation against a reference, each a place a wrong answer can start.
Choosing few contracted tables for a space and describing them so questions land on the right data.
Definitions written as executable SQL, such as a metric view's ratio-of-sums measure, instead of prose.
A parameterized example query or SQL function whose use labels a response Trusted, naming its source.
Data access for every Genie answer evaluated as the person asking; embedded credentials cover the warehouse only.
Running the benchmark per audience identity after each change, classifying failures and making one curation change per class.
A test question with class, expected SQL property, expected result property and whether the asker is authorized.
A reply that names the competing readings of an ambiguous question and asks which one is meant.
A question whose answer is not in the space's data or definitions, expected to be refused with a reason.
